text.text: Agents work inside sandboxes that hold no keys, reach only the hosts you expect, and cannot send anything anywhere. This page says how, what
A pasted key is the last resort.
Model-written code is the riskiest thing in the system, so it is the one place that never holds a secret. You connect your provider through
You approve access on your provider's own screen where the provider allows it. Where it does not, you can paste a key as a last resort: it i
Your key, when you must paste one, is encrypted
Starts the run and mints a short-lived token, valid for this workspace, this target, this budget and these models.
Holds a token that expires with the run
Where the agents read and write. Documents are mounted read-only. Only a short list of hosts can be reached.
Holds the token. No credential, ever
Turns the token into one call to your provider through your connection, checks the budget, and records the cost.
Reaches your provider one call at a time
Sees an ordinary call from your account. The bill lands with you, not with us.
The token dies with the run
It is scoped to one workspace, one target, a budget and a list of models. After the run, it opens nothing.
The budget is enforced outside the sandbox
The broker counts every call. When the cap is reached the run stops, whatever the agent wants.
A build fails if a credential leaks
A test searches the sandbox environment and its logs for credential patterns on every build.
Provider connections for Claude, OpenAI, Mistral and Gemini, run tokens, the broker and the egress allowlist ship with the first release.
The class decides who may read it.
A class is set when a document comes in and shown on every row of the ledger. Before you launch, the plan tells you which provider will read
Websites, filings, press, anything anyone can open.
Your ledger, with the source id and the date retrieved.
What the target shared with you: decks, data-room exports, financials, call notes.
Only providers that do not retain or train on your traffic, under a data processing agreement.
Your workspace only. Deleted with the target. Exports are watermarked.
Your thesis, partner notes, term sheets, references.
Same as above, and only for the targets and runs you allow.
Your vault, hosted by us and encrypted in your browser, or kept in Obsidian from Pro. A note reaches a run only when you share it.
Logs, traces and analytics carry ids and costs. They never carry evidence, prompts or keys.
Each control carries a status. At launch means it ships with the first release. Next and Later are on our roadmap, and we do not describe th
Sign-in by one-time email code, rate-limited and usable once. Roles per workspace. The database itself refuses to show one workspace the row
You approve access on your provider's own screen where the provider allows it, and you can revoke it at any time. Where it does not, a paste
One isolated sandbox per branch of a run. Evidence is mounted read-only. Each step reaches only the hosts it needs: search, the target's own
A founder deck can contain instructions. We treat every document as data, never as a command, and agents have no tool that could act on one.
Every tool call, decision and cost goes to an append-only log you can replay. Evidence goes when the target does, and a retention policy can
Links are scoped to the workspace and expire. File links are signed and short-lived. Exports carry the workspace and the date. Everything ca
Sandboxes hosted in the EU first. A Europe-only mode follows, where models are restricted to European regions or to a European provider.
Hosted by us and encrypted in your browser: we store ciphertext and cannot read it. From Pro, an Obsidian plugin keeps notes in your own vau
SAML sign-on for the whole team, and an audit log of who opened what, for the Fund plan.
These are rules built into the product, not promises in a policy.
Hold or read your provider credentials.
Send, post or email anything. Agents draft, people send.
Reach a host that is not on the list for that step.
Write a claim without a source, unless it is graded C and says so.
Spend past the budget you set.
Give a verdict without a person approving it at the gate.
We would rather say so than imply otherwise. Below is what is in place and what we are working toward, so you can judge whether it is enough
We sign one with you on request, and hold one with each subprocessor listed below.
Content security policy, rate limits, token and egress tests, a test deck that carries hostile instructions, dependency scanning, and key ro
A written process, and a public page showing the health of the service.
United States. Europe sandboxes follow, then a Europe-only mode.
Budgeted for the second year. It is a prerequisite for the Fund plan.
The model providers you connect are not our subprocessors. They run on your own accounts, under your terms.
Traces and logs, with no document content
Product analytics, on public and onboarding pages
Provider authorisation, so we never hold your keys
Claude, OpenAI, Mistral and Gemini, on your own accounts
Send your security review with the deal. We reply with the architecture, the data flow and the status of every control, before the first cal
Skilled agents, orchestrated for evidence. Built by operator-investors, for operator-investors.
